name: Obtain bid and performance bonds
summary: Public owners in Canada require a contractor to back its tender with a bid bond, usually 10% of the bid, and a surety's agreement to provide performance and labour and material payment bonds if it wins; Ontario requires both final bonds at 50% of the price on public contracts of $500,000 or more. The estimator spots the bonding requirement in the tender and sends a request to the treasury manager, who checks it against the company's bonding line, asks the broker for the bond, checks the wording and has it signed and sealed. After an award the treasury manager obtains the final bonds and delivers them to the owner with the signed contract. Delays come from large or unusual jobs that need the surety's underwriter, from errors in bond wording found late, and from originals that must be signed, sealed and couriered before a tender closes.

baseline.org_archetype: A national Canadian general contractor bidding about 22 stipulated price tenders a month, with a bonding line from a surety arranged through a broker.
baseline.notes: Most bid bonds are issued by the broker under the surety's power of attorney within the line; jobs above the single-job limit or outside the usual work go to the surety's underwriter.

trigger: An estimator finds a bonding requirement in a tender, or a contract award requires the final performance and labour and material payment bonds.
end_state: The signed and sealed bond is in the bid package or delivered to the owner, and is recorded in the bond register, or the surety declines the request.

volume.seasonality: Public tenders peak from February to June; fewer requests in August and December.

evidence.note: About 22 stipulated price bids a month (process map) each need a bid bond and agreement to bond, plus final bonds on about 60% of about 10 awards a month and occasional private or construction management bonds; gives about 30 to 35 requests.

surge.cause: Spring public tender season and fiscal year-end tender releases by public owners

evidence.note: Estimate based on public owners releasing capital tenders before the construction season.
About 45 to 60 minutes per request including line checks, broker emails, wording checks and the bond register.
Reads the tender's bonding clauses and fills in the request form.
Places the original bond in the sealed bid package or uploads the e-bond.
Signs and seals bonds as the company's signing officer.

systems.name: Public tender and bid portals (MERX, Bids&Tenders, Biddingo, provincial portals)
Construction ERP (job cost, general ledger, payables, receivables, payroll)
Take-off and estimating software with Excel bid sheets

steps.name: Prepare the bond request
steps.description: The estimator reads the tender's instructions to bidders and supplementary conditions, notes the bid security amount, the agreement to bond and the final bond percentages and forms, and fills in the company's bond request form with the owner, project, closing date and estimated price.

error.defect_description: Wrong obligee name, bond amount or form noted from the tender or an addendum missed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Check the request against the bonding line
steps.description: The treasury manager logs the request in the bond register and compares the bid price and the work on hand with the single-job and aggregate limits of the bonding line and the type of work and province the surety normally supports.

control.basis: Surety bonding line terms: single-job and aggregate limits

next.condition: over the single-job limit or unusual work

evidence.note: Sureties assess capital, capacity and character; the share needing underwriting is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare an underwriting submission
steps.description: The treasury manager writes a submission to the surety through the broker with the project description, estimate summary, schedule, contract terms, current work-in-progress schedule and latest financial statements.

evidence.note: Surety underwriting considers capital, capacity and character; the submission contents and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Surety underwriter reviews the job
steps.description: The surety's underwriter reviews the submission, may ask questions about the estimate, subcontractor bonding or contract risk, and approves the bond, approves it with conditions, or declines.

control.basis: Surety underwriting authority for jobs above the agent's power of attorney

next.condition: declined; company does not bid or finds a joint venture partner

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Send the bid bond request to the broker
steps.description: The treasury manager emails the broker the request form, the owner's bid bond form if one is prescribed, and the tender closing date and delivery method.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Broker issues the bid bond and agreement to bond
steps.description: The broker prepares the bid bond, usually 10% of the bid, and the surety's consent or agreement to provide final bonds, signed and sealed by the surety's attorney-in-fact, and sends originals or an electronic bond.

evidence.note: Bid bond terms from the federal standard form and Canadian Underwriter; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the bond wording
steps.description: The treasury manager compares the bond with the tender: obligee name, project name and tender number, bond amount or percentage, form, dates, seals and signatures, because a defective bid bond can disqualify the bid.

control.basis: Tender instructions: bid security in the required form or the bid is non-compliant

evidence.note: Bid bond terms from the federal standard form and Canadian Underwriter; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request a corrected bond
steps.description: The treasury manager emails the broker the correction needed and the deadline, and the broker reissues the bond before the tender closes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Sign and seal the bid bond
steps.description: The chief financial officer, as signing officer, signs the bond as principal and applies the corporate seal, with a witness signature where the form requires it.

control.basis: Company signing authority; bond form requires principal's signature and seal

evidence.note: The federal bid bond form is signed and sealed by principal and surety with a witness; who signs is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Place the bond in the bid package
steps.description: The bid coordinator puts the original bond and agreement to bond in the sealed bid envelope, or uploads the electronic bond to the tender portal, and confirms it on the bid checklist before closing.

error.defect_description: Bond left out of the envelope or uploaded to the wrong portal slot.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Record the bid bond in the register
steps.description: The treasury manager records the bond number, amount, obligee and closing date in the bond register so the broker can track bonds outstanding and release them when the tender is awarded to someone else.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Request final bonds after the award
steps.description: The treasury manager sends the broker the award letter, contract price, the owner's performance and labour and material payment bond forms (Ontario Forms 31 and 32 or the owner's own) and the date the owner needs them.

control.basis: Ontario Construction Act s.85.1: performance and labour and material payment bonds of at least 50% on public contracts of $500,000 or more

evidence.note: 50% performance and 50% labour and material payment bonds on Ontario public contracts of $500,000 or more and on federal contracts; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Surety issues the final bonds
steps.description: The broker and surety prepare the performance bond and labour and material payment bond on the required forms, checking the contract against the agreement to bond given at tender, and send the signed and sealed originals.

evidence.note: 50% performance and 50% labour and material payment bonds on Ontario public contracts of $500,000 or more and on federal contracts; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the final bonds against the contract
steps.description: The treasury manager checks contract price, percentages, obligee, project description, form and dates on both bonds against the executed contract and the owner's requirements.

control.basis: Prescribed bond forms under the Ontario Construction Act and the contract's security requirements

evidence.note: 50% performance and 50% labour and material payment bonds on Ontario public contracts of $500,000 or more and on federal contracts; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign and seal the final bonds
steps.description: The chief financial officer signs both bonds as principal and applies the corporate seal so that the originals can go to the owner with the executed contract.

control.basis: Company signing authority for bonds and contracts

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Deliver the bonds to the owner
steps.description: The treasury manager couriers the original bonds to the owner's contract office with the signed contract or a cover letter and keeps scanned copies in the project file.

evidence.note: Federal tenders require the contract and final bonds within 14 days after the forms are presented; delivery time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Owner accepts the bonds
steps.description: The owner's contract administrator checks the bonds and confirms acceptance, or asks for a correction, before releasing the contract for signature or allowing work to start.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

steps.name: Record the bonds and the premium
steps.description: The treasury manager records both bonds in the register, updates the work-on-hand schedule the surety uses to track the line, and codes the broker's premium invoice to the job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

exceptions.name: Job needs surety underwriting
exceptions.description: The bid exceeds the single-job limit or is unusual work, so the surety's underwriter must approve it; a few are declined.

exceptions.name: Bond wording error
exceptions.description: The bond names the wrong obligee or amount and must be reissued before closing.

exceptions.name: Final bond correction
exceptions.description: The owner or treasury finds the wrong form or amount on a final bond and the surety reissues it.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from bond request to bond in the bid package or delivered to the owner
benchmarks.population: Bid and final bond requests of a Canadian general contractor with an established bonding line

evidence.note: Bid bonds within the line are usually turned around in one to three days; final bonds take one to two weeks. No published benchmark found.

benchmarks.unit: % of the bid price (federal form, capped at $2,000,000)
% of contract price for each of the performance and labour and material payment bonds
benchmarks.population: Ontario public contracts of $500,000 or more

pain_points.description: Requests arrive a day or two before tender closing, leaving little time to fix a wrong obligee or amount.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

pain_points.description: Original bonds must be wet-signed, sealed and couriered, so the CFO's availability and courier times hold up bids and contract execution.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Canadian contractor surety practice through a bonding broker.

pain_points.description: Large or unusual jobs wait days for the surety's underwriter, which can rule out a bid.

evidence.note: Surety prequalification acts as a filter on contractors' capacity.

sources.title: Bid bond: PWGSC-TPSGC 504
sources.supports: Federal bid bond for 10% of the bid amount up to $2,000,000; void if the bidder signs the contract and provides 50% performance and 50% labour and material payment bonds within 14 days after the forms are presented (tender acceptance within 60 days); signed and sealed by principal and surety with a witness.

sources.title: Bonding basics: Sureties can reduce risk and ensure payments to subcontractors and suppliers, says SAC representative
sources.supports: Ontario Construction Act requires 50% performance and 50% labour and material payment bonds on public contracts of $500,000 or more signed after 1 July 2018; sureties assess capital, capacity and character; 2018 was the worst year for surety claims with a 105.6% net loss ratio.

sources.title: Building on a promise: construction surety bonds
sources.supports: Bid bond binds bidder and surety to enter the formal contract; performance bond and labour and material payment bond bought together after award; labour and material bond example limited to 50% of contract value; claimants can claim directly against the surety.

assumptions: The quarterly and annual reporting of financial statements and work in progress to the surety that keeps the bonding line open is a standing activity, not a per-request step; it is mentioned in s02 and s18 only.
The bond broker is treated as part of the surety external party; the organisation file has no separate broker.
The CFO signs bonds and the bid coordinator places them in the bid package, although the process map lists only the treasury manager and estimator.
Treasury-manager steps run on office hours, so a request that arrives late in the day waits overnight; this is included in the queue waits.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.
